overview: Guinea-Bissau is a small country on the Atlantic coast of West Africa. Its capital and largest city is Bissau. Guinea-Bissau won independence from Portugal in 1973–74 after an armed struggle, and Portuguese is the official language. Cashew nuts are its main export.

geography.text: Guinea-Bissau is low-lying, with a coastline cut by wide river mouths and mangroves. Offshore lies the Bijagós Archipelago, dozens of islands rich in wildlife, including hippos that swim in the sea and nesting sea turtles.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Hot and humid, with a rainy season.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: Saltwater hippos and turtles in the Bijagós.

history.text: The region was part of the Kaabu kingdom, linked to the Mali Empire. Portugal traded along the coast from the 1400s and later made it a colony. Amílcar Cabral led a war of independence from 1963, and Guinea-Bissau declared independence in 1973, recognised by Portugal in 1974. The country has had many coups since.

events.title: Independence war
events.text: The PAIGC begins its armed struggle.

events.title: Cabral killed
events.text: Amílcar Cabral is assassinated months before independence is declared.

government.text: Guinea-Bissau has had many coups and attempted coups since independence; in November 2025 the military seized power again. The country has struggled with instability for decades.

economy.text: Guinea-Bissau is one of the world's largest producers of cashew nuts, which make up almost all of its exports. Most people are farmers.

culture.text: The Bijagós Islands, an archipelago of 88 islands, have their own culture in which women traditionally hold important roles. Kriol, a Portuguese-based creole, is the common language.

items.title: Bijagós
items.text: Islands listed as a UNESCO biosphere reserve.

subsections.title: Food
subsections.text: Jollof rice and fish with palm oil.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: Carnival in Bissau is a big celebration.

sport.text: Football is the most popular sport, and Guinea-Bissau played at the Africa Cup of Nations for the first time in 2017.

didYouKnow: The Bijagós Islands are home to saltwater hippos.
Guinea-Bissau is one of the world's largest producers of cashew nuts.

keyPeople.name: Amílcar Cabral
keyPeople.text: Led the struggle against Portuguese rule.
